name: The Sassi and the Park of the Rupestrian Churches of Matera
description: In the southern Italian region of Basilicata, the city of Matera is built into a ravine, and its two old districts, Sasso Caveoso and Sasso Barisano, are a maze of dwellings carved into the rock. People have lived in these caves since the Palaeolithic, making it one of the Mediterranean's most intact cave-dwelling towns. Wander the stepped lanes and look across the gorge to the rock-cut churches in the surrounding park.
